content:
mia: heads-up, seeing an odd regression on the quantized bring-up job for model-x-4bit. eval CI passed but dashboard shows metric drift on 'answer_exact_match' for promptset 'customer-qa-v2'. suspect promptset leakage or shard mixup.

alex: can you paste the runner command + logs? is this only on the 4-bit branch or also fp16?

mia: reproducer command i used: `./tools/run_eval.sh --model model-x-4bit --promptset customer-qa-v2 --shard 2025-09-01`
```
mia: [log excerpt]
2025-09-10T14:01:02 Runner starting shard=2025-09-01 prompt_count=12
2025-09-10T14:01:04 Loaded fixture checksum: abc123def
2025-09-10T14:01:05 WARNING: potential overlap with synthetic fixtures detected: fixture ids [synth-104, synth-231]
2025-09-10T14:01:08 Eval finished: exact_match=0.82 (expected ~0.88)
```

priya: hmm i think i saw something similar last week. our leakage_check CI job uses shard labels like `shard=2025-09-01` but the synthetic generator outputs `shard=2025-09-01.synthetic`. the mismatch means the leakage script didn't run on the produced artifacts.

sam: eval-bot just posted the artifacts for that run: `s3://redwood-evals/model-x/1764201234/` — i downloaded the fixtures and the synthetic ids are interleaved with real ones. quick grep shows synthetic ids prefixed `synth-` inside the main fixture file.

```
sam: cat fixtures/2025-09-01.json | jq '.items[] | select(.id|test("^synth-")) | .id' | head
"synth-97"
"synth-104"
"synth-231"
```

yun: proposed quick mitigation: 1) make the leakage_check script robust to suffixes (`.synthetic`) and strip them when matching shards, 2) add a strict checksum assert in eval-runner that compares fixture manifest -> expected manifest and fails the job if any synthetic ids are present, and 3) add a CI gate that refuses merges if `--fail-on-leakage` isn't exercised in the PR pipeline.

alex: agree. also for the quantization signal we should isolate: run the same seed on fp16 vs 4bit with `--no-async-batching` to remove runtime batching variance. we should add a lightweight AB test in the dashboard comparing unquantized vs quantized outputs on the same prompt subset.

priya: jotting down the minimal changes:
```
- ci/jobs/leakage_check.yml: match: "shard: '.*'" -> stripSuffix(".synthetic")
- tools/leakage_check.py: return non-zero exit code if any synthetic ids found in shard manifest
- eval-runner: add --fail-on-leakage flag (defaults to true in CI)
- dashboards/qa: add panel showing exact_match by quantization variant
```

mia: can someone pick up the CI change? i can do the eval-runner assert. timeline: hope to have CI fix + runner assert in by EOD tomorrow so we can re-run the canary suite.

sam: i'll open a small PR to adjust the S3 artifact naming and add a test that generates a `.synthetic` suffix and asserts the leakage job flags it. pinging @priya for review.

priya: on it, will review and add a unit test for tools/leakage_check.py. also we'll add an integration step in the PR pipeline that runs `./tools/leakage_check.py --shard $CI_SHARD` against generated fixtures.

eval-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/canary/model-x/1764201234/ (checksums: fixtures_manifest=abc123def, manifest_expected=abc123def) :white_check_mark:

ci-bot: CI pipeline: leakage_check (skipped) -> eval-run (failed) -> notify #eng-ml. reason: leakage_check skipped due to shard label mismatch.

yun: follow-up items (short):
- [mia] add checksum assert in eval-runner, create `--fail-on-leakage` flag (ETA: tomorrow EOD)
- [sam] PR to normalize artifact shard tags and add canary for `.synthetic` suffix (ETA: today)
- [priya] review leakage_check tests and add CI integration step (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- [alex] add dashboard AB panel and run the isolated fp16 vs 4bit comparison (ETA: 48h)

mia: thanks all. once CI fix lands i'll kick off a full canary: `./tools/run_eval.sh --canary --models model-x fp16,model-x-4bit --promptset customer-qa-v2 --seed 42 --no-async-batching`. let's treat the current exact_match delta as a blocker until we confirm it's not data leakage. :lock: :eyes:

alex: noted. will coordinate with analytics to surface per-prompt diffs so we can triage if flips are concentrated on a small subset.

sam: adding labels to the thread: `leakage`, `ci`, `quantization`, `canary`.

mia: closing loop — pls post PR links here when ready.

(practical note: thread intentionally short on replies; we'll follow up with formal postmortem if the canary re-run shows persistent regression)
